sections.html:
Newberry County lies in central South Carolina, with the city of Newberry as its seat and largest community. The 2020 census counted 37,719 residents in 15,039 households, and the 2025 estimate is 39,561. About 30,400 parcels are on the books, mobile and manufactured homes included, so most sales are between local buyers and sellers.

Part of the county falls inside the Belfast Wildlife Management Area and the Sumter National Forest, which limits how much land can be built on or bought. Many houses date from the mill era and sit on farm-to-market roads. Original wiring, plumbing and roofs are common, and those are the systems a buyer's lender asks about.

Jobs are concentrated in a few plants. A layoff or relocation can leave a household selling fast, often with tax and mortgage payments already behind.

sections.h2: Which Newberry County offices handle property tax
sections.html:
The Assessor and the Delinquent Tax Collector share one address: 1512 Martin Street, Newberry, SC 29108. County administration is at 1309 College Street.

OfficePhone and hours
Assessor803-321-2125, option 1; assessorsoffice@newberrycounty.gov; 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays
Delinquent Tax Collector(803) 321-2128; 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays
County administration803-321-2100; 1309 College Street

The Assessor keeps ownership, valuation and assessment records for all real property. Forms are available for legal residence, mailing address change, agricultural use and a Notice of Objection.

sections.h2: Penalties on a Newberry County tax bill
sections.html:
Late bills follow the state schedule in S.C. Code 12-45-180. That adds 3 percent starting January 16, another 7 percent on February 2, and another 5 percent on March 17, when the Treasurer may also issue a tax execution. Check the dates against your own bill.

The Delinquent Tax Office collects overdue taxes through every legal channel, including bankruptcy claims in federal court and claims filed with the Probate Court. For an inherited house, that means an estate with unpaid tax can find a claim waiting in probate.

Some personal property accounts are placed with American Financial Credit Services. Once that happens, the county cannot take payment until the firm is paid, and the firm's fee goes on top.

Newberry County sells delinquent properties at an annual tax sale held at Piedmont Technical College's Newberry campus, 1922 Wilson Road. Bidders register in the morning before the sale starts and can pre-register in person at 1512 Martin Street or by email with a copy of photo ID.

  • Properties are advertised for three consecutive weeks in The Newberry Observer before the sale.
  • Mobile homes are included in the yearly sale.
  • Call the Delinquent Tax Collector for the current year's date and time.

Under S.C. Code 12-51-90 the owner can redeem within twelve months of the sale. Interest is 3 percent of the bid in the first quarter, 6 in the second, 9 in the third and 12 in the fourth. If nobody redeems, the buyer receives a deed. An owner who sees a sale coming can sell first, and the title company pays the county from the proceeds.

Send a Notice of Objection to the Assessor. State law sets the deadline at 90 days after the assessor mails the notice. Call the office to confirm the date on your notice.

The statute covers objections to fair market value, special use value or the assessment ratio. An owner who never received a notice may appeal in writing at any time. Filing before the first penalty date applies to the current year, and filing later applies to the next one.

sections.h2: Legal residence and the 4 percent ratio
sections.html:
New owners who live in the house should file early for the legal residence classification. The 4 percent ratio applies to an owner-occupied home that is not rented more than 72 days a year, and the application must be filed before the first penalty date.

Miss it and the 6 percent ratio applies for that year, which can overstate the tax portion of a buyer's mortgage payment. A seller can help a buyer by mentioning the form up front.

Land used to commercially grow crops or timber can qualify for agricultural use valuation. If part of the land you are selling carries that status, ask the Assessor what a change of use or a sale does to the value before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What a Newberry County seller should do first
sections.html:
Start by finding out exactly what is owed and which office holds it. One short call to the right office can save weeks later.

  • Call the Assessor at 803-321-2125, option 1, to confirm the owner of record, the mailing address and whether the legal residence form is on file.
  • Call the Delinquent Tax Collector at (803) 321-2128 if any year is past due, and ask for a payoff good through the expected closing date.
  • If the owner has died, ask whether the Delinquent Tax Office has filed a claim with the Probate Court.
  • Check whether a tax sale notice has been advertised in The Newberry Observer.

Unpaid taxes do not prevent a sale. The title company sends the county its balance from the seller's proceeds at closing, so the seller needs a current payoff in hand before the closing date. Ask the Delinquent Tax Office for it in writing if possible.

Give the title company three things early: the payoff figure, the parcel details and the date you hope to close. If the closing date moves, ask for an updated payoff, since penalties added on January 16, February 2 or March 17 change the amount.

A cash sale skips the lender appraisal, the buyer's repair requests and the wait on a mortgage approval. For an older mill-era house with original systems, or an estate with a probate claim attached, that shorter path can matter more than a slightly higher listing price.

sections.h2: What to bring to the office
sections.html: Take photo ID and the property address to 1512 Martin Street. If you are handling an estate, bring proof that you may act for the owner. Ask each office what it needs before you drive over, since the Assessor and the Delinquent Tax Collector handle different records even though they share a building.

faqs.q: Where is the Newberry County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: 1512 Martin Street, Newberry, SC 29108. Call 803-321-2125, option 1. The office is open 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: Who collects delinquent taxes in Newberry County?
faqs.a: The Delinquent Tax Collector, at 1512 Martin Street. The number is (803) 321-2128.

faqs.q: When is the Newberry County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is held once a year at Piedmont Technical College's Newberry campus. Call the Delinquent Tax Collector for this year's date and registration time.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Newberry County assessment?
faqs.a: File a written Notice of Objection with the Assessor. State law allows 90 days from the mailing of the assessment notice.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Newberry County house that owes taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the proceeds at closing. Get a payoff from the Delinquent Tax Office before the closing date.
